jobs.title: Senior Vice President, Enterprise Technology & Compliance
jobs.description:
About Kindsight:

Kindsight builds technology that helps fundraisers make a difference. For decades, Kindsight has supported the education, healthcare, and nonprofit sectors with fundraising tools and the largest charitable giving database on the market. And as the giving sector evolves, so does Kindsight. As the leader in fundraising intelligence, Kindsight leverages real-time data and AI to help thousands of organizations around the world identify, manage, and engage with donors - at any scale. With purpose-built CRMs that corral all of that donor information and campaign tracking into one place, donor prospect research tools that offer proactive insights and real-time donor intel, and generative AI that creates personalized, meaningful content drafts at scale, Kindsight’s product suite is truly changing the game for donor fundraising.

Position Summary:

We are seeking a strategic technology executive with extensive experience leading enterprise technology, cybersecurity, and compliance within a growing SaaS business. This leader will enable the business through modern, secure, and scalable technology while accelerating Kindsight's transformation into an AI-native company. Working closely with the CTO, you will lead the enterprise technology strategy that enables the business while complementing the company's product and engineering strategy. You will hire, lead, and develop a high-performing Enterprise Technology organization spanning IT, cybersecurity, and compliance. You will be responsible for ensuring budget discipline while optimizing technology investments and operating costs. In addition to enterprise technology responsibilities, this role will ensure the business operates within legal, regulatory, and ethical boundaries—especially around data, privacy, and global software regulations.

What You’ll Do:

AI Strategy

Lead the development and execution of Kindsight’s internal enterprise AI adoption strategy, partnering with executive leadership to improve productivity, automate business processes, and deliver measurable operational and financial outcomes. .
Translate strategy into a clear technology roadmap across infrastructure, systems, and enterprise applications, supporting an AI-native operating model and a scalable, cost-effective SaaS environment.
Lead enterprise technology transformation initiatives, including Lead-to-Cash, business systems modernization, business intelligence, and AI enablement, with accountability for execution, organizational adoption, and measurable business outcomes. .
Lead technology due diligence and integration for acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and other corporate initiatives.

IT Operations and Business Systems

Own Kindsight’s enterprise technology ecosystem: business systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS), infrastructure, networks, collaboration platforms, and enterprise data architecture.
Oversee day-to-day IT operations and end-user services, ensuring reliability, performance, and scalability, with strong service management practices including SLAs and incident management.

Security and Risk

Own Kindsight’s enterprise information security program, establishing and maintaining appropriate security policies, controls, monitoring, and risk mitigation practices across corporate technology environments.
Identify and manage technology risks, including vulnerabilities, third-party exposure, and operational risk.
Oversee incident response, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.

Compliance and Privacy

Lead Kindsight’s information security and technology compliance programs, establishing governance, policies, controls, and audit readiness aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and recognized frameworks, including SOC 2 and ISO 27001.
Establish governance for AI usage, third-party technology risk, and enterprise data management.
Drive audit readiness, coordinate internal and external audits, and serve as the key contact for auditors, regulators, and enterprise customers.
Oversee data privacy practices and monitor regulatory developments affecting SaaS and CRM platforms.

Partnership and Culture

Partner with Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Sales, and Customer Success to establish consistent security and compliance standards, support customer security assessments, and ensure appropriate governance across enterprise and customer-facing technology. Provide clear, concise updates to executive leadership on risk, security posture, and compliance status.

People and Budget

Hire, lead, and develop IT and compliance teams, including directors and managers, with clear accountability, performance expectations, and succession planning.
Manage the IT and compliance budget and oversee vendor selection, contracts, and performance, ensuring technology investments deliver business value.
Build a culture of security, compliance, and responsible data use, including employee training programs.

What We’re Looking For:

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in enterprise technology, cybersecurity, or IT operations, including significant executive-level responsibility within a complex SaaS or technology organization.
In-depth knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NIST), compliance standards (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.), and data protection.
Proven executive leadership of enterprise-wide business transformation initiatives, serving as the accountable executive responsible for strategy, governance, planning, execution, and organizational adoption.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise transformation roadmaps, including program governance, milestones, dependencies, and executive reporting.
Proven experience creating and leading enterprise-wide communication and change management strategies that keep employees, leaders, and stakeholders informed and aligned throughout transformational initiatives.
Track record of leading complex cross-functional initiatives across Technology, Product, Finance, Operations, Sales, and Customer Success while driving organizational alignment and measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated experience managing enterprise technology budgets, optimizing vendor expenditures, and allocating resources to deliver measurable business value.
Deep understanding of enterprise architecture, cloud solutions (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), and scalable infrastructure management.
Strategic Vision: Ability to align technology roadmap with business objectives to enhance competitive advantage.
Demonstrated experience deploying AI technologies to improve productivity, automate business processes, and drive measurable business outcomes across enterprise functions.
Leadership: Exceptional team leadership, mentoring, and talent development skills, with experience managing remote or distributed teams.
Communication: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to convey complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and the Board of Directors.
Vendor Management: Strong negotiation skills for managing relationships with strategic technology partners and vendors.
Experience leading enterprise technology within a high-growth SaaS organization, preferably in a private equity-backed environment.
Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or IT, Cybersecurity or Information Systems and MBA or equivalent is an asset.

What Success Looks Like

Accelerate responsible AI adoption across Kindsight's business functions, delivering measurable improvements in productivity and operational efficiency.
Maintain a secure, highly available enterprise technology environment.
Strengthen the company's security and compliance posture.
Optimize technology investments while improving employee productivity.
Build and develop a high-performing enterprise technology organization.

What’s in it for you?

Compensation Range: $300,000-$350,000 CAD/USD OTE annually, based on experience, market benchmarks and role complexity. We aim to offer fair, competitive pay that reflects your skills and the market.
Time to unplug: Vacation, flex days, volunteer time and a team-wide year-end wellness shutdown.
Whole-person health: Comprehensive health and dental, 24/7 virtual doctor visits and flexible wellness stipends.
Flexibility first: Digital-first remote setup with built-in “work from anywhere” travel flexibility.
Investment in you: Departmental professional development budgets and company-matched retirement savings.
A team that celebrates: Paid parental leave, peer recognition rewards and company-wide celebrations.

jobs.title: VP, Consulting & Transformation
jobs.description:
Domaine is a global digital commerce and transformation partner for ambitious and beloved brands. We are the world’s largest independent Shopify partner. We are also a growing team of strategists, designers, engineers and specialists who help brands decide where to invest, build what comes next, and run it at scale across platforms, channels and AI. As pioneers and not just participants in our industry, we are inspired to write, break, and re-write the rules for a new generation of commerce.

The VP, Consulting leads Domaine’s Consulting practice and holds a seat on the Craft Leadership team. The practice brings together multiple disciplines: Strategy, AI and Transformation Advisory, CRM and Lifecycle, Conversion Rate Optimization, and SEO/GEO/AEO. This role owns consulting as a commercial function as well as an advisory one. It is how Domaine moves from being chosen for a platform build to being chosen for the business outcomes.

This role does not receive a brief and execute it. It takes in a conversation with a prospect or existing client, specific or vague, and discerns the goals, the real needs, the gaps, the path, and the teams and skills required to get there. It then builds the plan and the trust to see it funded. It works in lockstep with Client Partners, Creative, Sales and Engineering, and brings commercial instinct to every recommendation: what should change, why it will grow the client’s business, what it will cost, and what it will return.

Responsibilities

Consulting Leadership

Lead senior engagements for clients including digital and AI transformation, platform and replatforming decisions, international expansion, B2B, retail and POS, loyalty, marketplace, data, and operating model.
Run structured Discovery across business objectives, customer insight, data, technology, organization and operating model. Translate it into goals, needs, gaps, a sequenced path, and the capabilities and skills required.
Build the business case that turns a roadmap into funded work and prioritization by business impact, customer impact, level of effort, and dependency.
Produce multi-year roadmaps to show the art of the possible and how they get there.
Recommend what Domaine should and should not do. Where a client’s best path goes beyond our delivery, build the partner or co-delivery model rather than shrinking the recommendation.

Retention, Account Expansion, and Commercial Growth

Own the 1, 3 or 5 year plan for every top-tier retained client, tied to their stated business goals. A launch is the beginning of our relationship with the client, not the end.
Chair or co-chair Growth Councils and QBRs with the Client Partner, run as forward-looking conversations with explicit ROI accountability rather than a retrospective of work delivered.
Support the orchestration of a unified team for every retained client, synthesizing strategy, AI and transformation, CRM and lifecycle, Conversion Rate Optimization, SEO/GEO/AEO, Design, and Technology perspectives into a single narrative. Help evolve accounts from single-threaded delivery to multi-service relationships.
Provide the strategic input and human judgment layer on client health and monthly intelligence reporting, on top of AI-generated analysis.
Ensure consulting hours are named, scoped, and priced into retainers and new builds rather than absorbed into the account.
Join pursuits for strategic accounts, bringing senior transformational thinking into the room alongside Sales and Client Partners.
Help shape scope before pricing on complex or multi-discipline engagements, so the approach differentiates the proposal rather than reading as a deliverable list.
Own the strategic spine of Domaine’s pitch narrative, positioning Domaine as a digital services partner and not only a platform implementer, and keep it current as the market moves.

Practice Leadership and Partner Advisory

Fluent in every discipline they lead. Knows Strategy, CRO, CRM and Lifecycle, SEO/GEO/AEO and our emerging AI services from the inside: the KPIs that run each one and how each should be applied to project and retained work.Own quality, methodology and playbooks, team structure, performance management, and day-to-day operation.
Carry practice margin and utilization targets.
Build the documentation, frameworks, and evaluation criteria that let each discipline scale past the people currently doing the work.
Turn proven pilots, including managed services and Domaine Labs and AI Commerce capabilities, into standard offerings with defined scope and pricing.
Help shape Domaine’s point of view on the digital commerce stack beyond the storefront: search and discovery, personalization, lifecycle and messaging, loyalty, subscription, PIM, ERP, OMS, DAM, data, and the AI tooling layer around them.
Advise clients on whether their current stack supports their goals and competitive needs, and where to reinvest. Consulting evaluates whether the investment holds up against the client’s growth plan.

Practice and People Leadership

Support the enablement of applied AI so it shows up in client roadmaps as measurable, and bring AI-differentiated capability into sales conversations, including AI discoverability, agentic commerce operations, and partner stack advisory.
Redefine consulting and discipline deliverables for an AI-native workflow, with measurable impacts.
A leader the practice leads trust. Mentors the discipline leads, earns their confidence, and pushes each practice toward continual improvement and revenue growth.Set performance standards and build a bench that can operate without you in the room.
Hold the layer below accountable as leaders owning outcomes.

Qualifications

10+ years in consulting, strategy, or senior client leadership, with meaningful time in a client-facing senior role at an agency, digital consultancy, or consulting firm.
Track record of leading digital transformation engagements from an ambiguous problem to a funded roadmap to a delivered outcome.
Experience running a consulting or strategy function and a multi-discipline group: defining the offering, setting methodology, carrying a commercial number, and building and leading leaders.
Demonstrated experience building and defending a business case for a digital transformation initiative, including ROI modeling and prioritization frameworks.
Track record of growing retained or recurring revenue relationships, not only winning net-new business.
Strong command of the digital commerce growth model: demand generation, conversion, lifecycle and retention, merchandising and AOV, and the data that connects them. Enough depth to make credible recommendations and lead discipline leaders.
Fluency in the commerce ecosystem and the surrounding partner, app, and enterprise systems landscape.

Perks & Benefits

Competitive Healthcare with Dental & Vision
Retirement savings plan with employer matching
Competitive PTO policy with paid time off at end of year
Flexible working schedule
Remote-first culture
Home office stipend
Apple gear
Continued education and personal development opportunities

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

As Director, Operations
, you'll own Solink's end-to-end sales-to-deployment operating model, from the moment a deal closes to the point a customer is live, supported and generating recurring revenue. Our Deployment function has grown in scale, complexity and strategic importance, and this role exists to lead it into its next chapter.

You'll lead a team across three focus areas: Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Operations Enablement. You'll be accountable for the overall function and driving major automation and process-improvement initiatives and partnering with senior leaders across the organization to improve planning, quality, scalability and accountability.

This is an opportunity for an operations leader who's energized by building systems that scale, raising the bar on execution and connecting operational performance directly to ARR growth.

What You’ll Do

Own the sales-to-deployment operating model: Define and continuously improve how work flows from Sales through Deployment to Support, including handoffs, planning, capacity, quality standards and accountability at every stage.
Lead and develop a high-performing leadership team: Lead Managers across Deployment Execution, Optimization & Automation, and Enablement & Cross-Functional. Set clear goals, coach for growth and build a leadership bench that can scale with the business.
Drive operational transformation: Lead major automation, tooling and process-improvement initiatives that increase throughput, reduce cycle time and improve the customer deployment experience.
Deliver on ARR: Ensure deployments are executed on time and at quality so that contracted revenue converts to recurring revenue predictably. Own the metrics, forecasting and reporting that connect operations to financial outcomes.
Partner across the organization: Work closely with senior leaders in Sales, Customer Success, Support, Product and Finance to align on planning, resolve cross-functional friction and make Deployment a strategic lever for the business.
Establish governance and operational rigour: Set the standards, SOPs, KPIs and reporting cadence that give leadership clear visibility into deployment health, capacity and risk.
Oversee partner and field strategy: Guide how Solink works with installation partners and field resources, including partner enablement, performance management and relationship health.
Serve as the senior escalation point: Own resolution of high-impact customer and operational escalations, and turn recurring issues into systemic fixes.

Role Expectations

This is an M4 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level serve as a strategic advisor within a department, who is confident acting as their executive leader’s right hand within their functional area and is able to set cross-functional direction in collaboration with departments within the organization.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

Set the vision and multi-quarter roadmap for the Deployment function and translate it into clear priorities for your managers.
Operate with a high degree of autonomy, making decisions that shape how the function runs and how it interacts with the rest of the business.
Influence senior stakeholders across functions, building alignment on shared goals, processes and trade-offs.
Balance near-term delivery with long-term investment in automation, tooling and scalability.
Build a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement across the Deployment team.

What success looks like:

Deployment cycle times, on-time delivery and quality metrics improve measurably, and ARR from new deals is realized faster and more predictably.
Key automation and process-improvement initiatives are delivered, reducing manual effort and allowing the function to scale without proportional headcount growth.
Sales, Deployment, Support and other partners operate from a shared planning model with clear handoffs, visible accountability and fewer escalations.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

8+ years in operations, deployment, implementation or professional services, including 3+ years leading managers or multi-team functions.
A proven track record of designing and scaling an end-to-end operating model in a high-growth B2B technology, SaaS or hardware-enabled services environment.
Demonstrated success leading process-improvement and automation initiatives with measurable impact on efficiency, quality or revenue.
Strong analytical and business acumen, with experience owning KPIs, capacity planning and operational reporting tied to financial outcomes such as ARR.
Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills, with the credibility to influence senior leaders and drive alignment.

Nice-to-Have:

Experience in physical security, video surveillance, IoT or other field-deployed technology.
Experience managing installation partner or channel networks across multiple regions.
Familiarity with operations tooling and automation platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Asana, Jira, n8n or similar).
Background in Lean, Six Sigma or other formal continuous-improvement methodologies.

Security Requirements

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Compensation

The compensation range for this role is $156,696-195,870 CAD and includes a base salary plus a performance-based variable component.

We determine compensation based on the experience, skills, and impact you bring to the role.

For this position, we are hiring within the Proficient
range. Candidates in this range will demonstrate the ability to serve as a strategic advisor within their department, confidently acting as the senior leader's right hand within their functional area and setting cross-functional direction in collaboration with other departments across the organization.

Our Values

We do things the Solink way:

Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.
Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.
Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.

Why Solink?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.
Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.
Comprehensive benefits: Fully paid health & dental (no waiting period) + $500 health spending account.

Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.

About The Company

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
is the primary public electricity utility serving the Northwest Territories and plays a critical role in supporting the territory's economic development, community well-being, and energy security. As a crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of the Northwest Territories through NT Hydro, NTPC is responsible for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across one of the most geographically vast and operationally challenging jurisdictions in North America. The organization provides power to more than 43,000 residents across 27 communities and manages a diverse portfolio of hydroelectric, diesel, natural gas, solar, wind, and battery storage assets. With more than $650 million in assets and approximately 151 MW of generating capacity, NTPC operates a geographically dispersed and operationally diverse utility system across the Northwest Territories.

For more information, please download the full position profile: NTPC CEO Position Profile.pdf

Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for providing the strategic, operational, financial, and cultural leadership required to guide the Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC), Northwest Territories Hydro (NT Hydro), and their subsidiaries. The CEO will ensure the organizations effectively fulfill their commercial and public-service mandates while aligning with the strategic priorities of the Government of the Northwest Territories and the evolving needs of residents, communities, businesses, and industrial customers across the North.

The CEO will provide the leadership required to advance NTPC's mandate as the Northwest Territories' leading electricity utility while supporting the priorities of the Board of Directors and shareholder. Operating at the intersection of public policy, utility operations, infrastructure investment, and economic development, the CEO will guide the organization through a period of significant transformation as it addresses aging infrastructure, increasing energy demand, major capital investment requirements, and the transition toward a more sustainable and diversified energy future. This will require a strategic yet pragmatic leader who can establish a clear long-term direction while remaining accessible, hands-on when required, and closely connected to the operational realities of delivering critical utility services across the North.

Working within a highly regulated and publicly accountable environment, the CEO will balance the operational and commercial requirements of the Corporation with broader territorial priorities. This includes advancing strategic initiatives related to system reliability, affordability, renewable energy integration, Indigenous partnerships, economic development, and long-term energy security, while ensuring strong financial stewardship, operational excellence, and organizational performance. Preparing NTPC for future growth will be a central leadership mandate, requiring the CEO to ensure the Corporation has the people, leadership capacity, systems, infrastructure, partnerships, and financial readiness required to respond to increasing demand and emerging opportunities across the Northwest Territories.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, political acumen, and stakeholder leadership required to navigate a complex operating environment and build trusted relationships with government, regulators, Indigenous governments, communities, customers, employees, and industry partners. Beyond delivering operational and financial results, the CEO will be expected to foster a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement while positioning NTPC for long-term operational, financial, and environmental sustainability and ensuring the reliable delivery of affordable energy to communities across the Northwest Territories.

Education And Experience Requirements

Education and Professional Background

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, commerce or other related discipline.
Significant senior leadership experience within the utility sector or a similarly complex, capital-intensive, highly regulated environment.
Experience leading organizations with significant operational, infrastructure, stakeholder, and public accountability requirements will be highly valued.
Minimum of eight years of direct management experience, in a unionized work environment.
Previous experience providing advice to and receiving direction from a Board of Directors.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

The role is based at NTPC’s head office in Hay River and requires a visible leadership presence within the organization and community. Regular travel to Yellowknife and NTPC’s regional plants, offices, and communities throughout the Northwest Territories is required. This may include travel by small aircraft and extended stays due to weather or operational requirements. The demands of the role may also require work outside normal office hours.

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
is the primary public electricity utility serving the Northwest Territories and plays a critical role in supporting the territory's economic development, community well-being, and energy security. As a crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of the Northwest Territories through NT Hydro, NTPC is responsible for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across one of the most geographically vast and operationally challenging jurisdictions in North America. The organization provides power to more than 43,000 residents across 27 communities and manages a diverse portfolio of hydroelectric, diesel, natural gas, solar, wind, and battery storage assets. With more than $650 million in assets and approximately 151 MW of generating capacity, NTPC operates a geographically dispersed and operationally diverse utility system across the Northwest Territories.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for providing the strategic, operational, financial, and cultural leadership required to guide the Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC), Northwest Territories Hydro (NT Hydro), and their subsidiaries. The CEO will ensure the organizations effectively fulfill their commercial and public-service mandates while aligning with the strategic priorities of the Government of the Northwest Territories and the evolving needs of residents, communities, businesses, and industrial customers across the North.

The CEO will provide the leadership required to advance NTPC's mandate as the Northwest Territories' leading electricity utility while supporting the priorities of the Board of Directors and shareholder. Operating at the intersection of public policy, utility operations, infrastructure investment, and economic development, the CEO will guide the organization through a period of significant transformation as it addresses aging infrastructure, increasing energy demand, major capital investment requirements, and the transition toward a more sustainable and diversified energy future. This will require a strategic yet pragmatic leader who can establish a clear long-term direction while remaining accessible, hands-on when required, and closely connected to the operational realities of delivering critical utility services across the North.

Working within a highly regulated and publicly accountable environment, the CEO will balance the operational and commercial requirements of the Corporation with broader territorial priorities. This includes advancing strategic initiatives related to system reliability, affordability, renewable energy integration, Indigenous partnerships, economic development, and long-term energy security, while ensuring strong financial stewardship, operational excellence, and organizational performance. Preparing NTPC for future growth will be a central leadership mandate, requiring the CEO to ensure the Corporation has the people, leadership capacity, systems, infrastructure, partnerships, and financial readiness required to respond to increasing demand and emerging opportunities across the Northwest Territories.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, political acumen, and stakeholder leadership required to navigate a complex operating environment and build trusted relationships with government, regulators, Indigenous governments, communities, customers, employees, and industry partners. Beyond delivering operational and financial results, the CEO will be expected to foster a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement while positioning NTPC for long-term operational, financial, and environmental sustainability and ensuring the reliable delivery of affordable energy to communities across the Northwest Territories.

Education And Experience Requirements

Education and Professional Background

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, commerce or other related discipline.
Significant senior leadership experience within the utility sector or a similarly complex, capital-intensive, highly regulated environment.
Experience leading organizations with significant operational, infrastructure, stakeholder, and public accountability requirements will be highly valued.
Minimum of eight years of direct management experience, in a unionized work environment.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

The role is based at NTPC’s head office in Hay River and requires a visible leadership presence within the organization and community.
